name: LLVM lld for macOS (ld64.lld)
baseline: Apple ld-prime, the default linker with Xcode 15 or later, called through cc
verdict_reason: An older Chromium doc (2021 or earlier) reported lld 4x faster than Apple's old ld64, but Apple replaced ld64 with ld-prime in Xcode 15. Chromium's current docs say ld-prime is faster than lld for local arm64 macOS builds, by up to 4-6x, and Bevy's build config now keeps the default macOS linker for the same reason.
tier_reason: Chromium's build team measured on its own codebase; it is independent of Apple and contributes to LLD, so a result in ld-prime's favour is not self-serving. Detailed timings are in a bug tracker, not the doc.
claimed_speedup: Historic (older Chromium doc): lld 4x faster than ld64 linking Chromium Framework. Current: switching from lld to ld-prime gives up to a 4-6x speedup for local arm64 macOS Chromium builds
workload: Linking Chromium on macOS: local non-cross arm64 developer builds (current doc); Chromium Framework in symbol_level=0 release builds (2021 doc)
hardware: Apple silicon (arm64) Macs; models not stated
toolchain: Chromium's LLD from its clang package vs Apple ld-prime from Xcode
platforms: Mach-O port of lld; lld also covers ELF, COFF and Wasm
one_liner: LLVM's Mach-O linker: once 4x faster than Apple's ld64, now slower than Apple's ld-prime default on Apple silicon.
how_it_is_fast: lld's Mach-O port follows the same design as its ELF port, which beat Apple's older ld64 by a wide margin. Apple's rewritten linker, ld-prime, shipped with Xcode 15 and now leads on arm64 Macs, so the speed case for switching has reversed.
use_it_when: Cross-compiling to macOS from Linux, where Apple's linker is not available
Builds that need one linker across platforms or LTO with matching LLVM versions (Chromium's reasons for keeping LLD)
skip_it_when: Native arm64 macOS development on Xcode 15 or later: the default linker is faster
caveats: Chromium's doc gives a range ('up to 4-6x') without the underlying timings
Chromium is a very large C++ program; Rust binaries are usually smaller, so absolute savings are smaller
The doc does not date the benchmark
tradeoffs: Slower than the default linker on Apple silicon

evidence.quote: Recent benchmarks show that Apple's new linker (ld-prime) is faster than LLD for local macOS development
Supported only for local non-cross arm64 macOS builds (ARM Mac) to improve link speed (yielding up to a 4-6x speedup depending on configuration).
LLD is currently 4x faster at linking Chromium Framework than ld64
On macOS, the default linker yields higher performance than LLD and is used instead.
